title: UN Human Rights Office Reiterates Support for Ayotzinapa Families Amid CNDH Fallout
detail: The UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights in Mexico (ONU-DH) reiterated its commitment to continue accompanying the families of the 43 in the search for truth and justice, and defended the value of 'international assistance' after the CNDH's recommendation questioned the GIEI's work. The statement, issued days after the CNDH report, said 'a wound remains open' nearly 12 years after the disappearances.

media.caption: UN Human Rights Office in Mexico reaffirms support for the families of the 43

title: FGR to Present New Investigative Advances Following CNDH Controversy
detail: Following the backlash to the CNDH's recommendation and Sheinbaum's move to distance her government from it, the Attorney General's Office (FGR) signaled it would present new advances in the Ayotzinapa investigation in the coming days, as President Sheinbaum had previously indicated the government possessed findings it could not yet share publicly without authorization from the families.

media.caption: FGR expected to present new advances in the Ayotzinapa investigation
